newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Five Colombian rebels killed in latest clashes.
newsitem.headline: Five Colombian rebels killed in latest clashes.

text.p: Five leftist guerrillas died in the last two days as the Colombian army continued to repel one of the bloodiest rebel offensives in decades, military sources said on Thursday.
Counterinsurgency troops in northeastern Norte de Santander province killed three members of the People's Liberation Army on Wednesday, Maj. Gen. Rafael Hernandez said.

In northwestern Antioquia province, scene of some of the most bitter fighting in the last month, soldiers shot dead a militia member linked to the National Liberation Army (ELN) in the town of Segovia on Wednesday. The previous day another ELN militia man was killed near the same town.

During Wednesday's firefight in Segovia, the rebels set off a bomb, wounding one soldier and seven civilians. Small quantities of automatic weapons, pistols and radio equipment were seized by the military.

Colombia's largest and oldest guerrilla force, the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC), unleashed the most violent offensive in recent memory when it overran a military base in southern Putumayo province on Aug. 30, killing 27 soldiers and taking at least 60 prisoner, none of whom have been released.
The ELN, the second largest rebel force, declared an "armed strike" or nationwide offensive a week ago. Authorities estimated at least 60 guerrillas were killed in Antioquia over the weekend.

In an effort to break the stranglehold the rebels exercised by blockading some of the country's main highways, the military called in air strikes in some areas and announced it would escort trucks and buses along some of the most dangerous stretches.
